slides.title:
Sequence-Based Prediction of Single-Residue
Mutation Effects on PSI in Degron Assays and
Development of an Analysis Tool
slides.notes:
Official English title: Sequence-Based Prediction of Single-Residue Mutation Effects on PSI in Degron Assays and Development of an Analysis Tool
Official Vietnamese title: Dự đoán ảnh hưởng của đột biến amino acid đơn lên chỉ số PSI trong nghiên cứu degron và xây dựng công cụ phân tích

Research progress as of 7 November 2026. Student: Nguyen Thanh Trong, B2305615. Supervisor: Ho Quang Thai, Ph.D. This presentation reports development evidence, not an acceptance decision or wet-lab validation.

slides.title: From biology to prediction evidence
slides.subtitle: Full research report; detailed result tables are retained in the appendix
slides.notes: The appendix is for reference and need not be presented in full. Results are development evidence unless stated otherwise. Dates identify saved evidence snapshots.

items.heading: Biological foundations and prediction task
items.body: Protein → UPS → degron → mutation → ΔPSI

items.heading: Related work and experimental data
items.body: Assay, provenance, quality control and observation units

items.heading: Methods and evaluation design
items.body: Ridge, pLMs, CNN/mCNN, LoRA and leakage controls

items.heading: Available experimental results

slides.title: Proteins: amino-acid chains with cellular functions
slides.subtitle: A · Biological foundations
slides.notes: Proteins are chains of amino acids joined by peptide bonds. A residue is an amino acid within a chain; a peptide is a short segment. Here the model receives a 28-residue peptide, not the entire protein or its cellular environment. This schematic was drawn by CT553H and is not a measured structure.

slides.title: Stability must be defined by its measurement
slides.subtitle: A · Three related concepts describe different quantities
slides.notes: A single PSI value does not determine half-life or folding free energy. Reporter abundance can reflect several biological processes. CT553H predicts a specific assay endpoint.

items.heading: Protein abundance
items.body: The amount of protein at a given time depends on both synthesis and degradation.

items.heading: Protein lifetime
items.body: Turnover and half-life describe replacement or degradation over time.

items.heading: Structural stability
items.body: Thermodynamic stability concerns protein folding; it differs from reporter PSI.

slides.title: UPS: recognition, ubiquitination and degradation
slides.subtitle: A · Ubiquitin–Proteasome System
slides.notes: CT553H conceptual schematic: E1 activates ubiquitin, E2 carries it, E3 recognizes the substrate and catalyzes ubiquitin transfer, and the proteasome degrades appropriately tagged proteins. This simplified workflow does not identify the E3 responsible for a CT553H variant effect.

slides.title: A degron acts within a protein context
slides.subtitle: A · A sequence segment can contribute to targeting a protein for degradation
slides.notes: A degron is not the whole protein. Its activity can depend on exposure, structure, post-translational modifications and E3/cellular context. A peptide reporter may expose a segment buried in the native protein. The diagram is a conceptual schematic drawn for this report.

slides.title: A single substitution changes one residue
slides.subtitle: A · Wild type (WT): reference sequence; mutant: sequence after substitution
slides.notes: Wild type (WT) is the reference sequence; the mutant contains the substitution. The example is selected first by peptide_id, numerical position and mutant amino acid in the saturation table. WT: RSLHLPQLRFSRVDATAVTDVPFQRMHA; mutant: ASLHLPQLRFSRVDATAVTDVPFQRMHA. A substitution may disrupt a signal, create one or alter context; its effect cannot be inferred from amino-acid names alone.

slides.title: The GPS assay turns reporter behavior into data
slides.subtitle: A · HEK293T; GFP–28-AA peptide reporter; DsRed reference; six FACS bins
slides.notes: Global Protein Stability profiling uses a library of GFP-linked peptides. The GFP/DsRed ratio assigns cells to six FACS bins, then sequencing counts each construct in each bin. A constant C-terminal segment limits artificial C-degrons. This figure illustrates the workflow; it is not a new wet-lab image or measurement.

slides.title: PSI is a reporter index on a scale from 1 to 6
slides.subtitle: A · Protein Stability Index in the Zhang assay; not a time unit
slides.notes: build_psi.py normalizes counts by bin and computes a weighted mean of bin indices. p(b) is the normalized proportion of a construct in bin b, summing to 1; PSI=sum b*p(b). Higher PSI indicates a more stable reporter within this assay. This is not a splicing PSI or a generic protein-stability measure.

slides.title: WT and mutant measurements define ΔPSI
slides.subtitle: A → B · Real R1A record; displayed values are rounded
slides.notes: Saturation has two halves, sat_a and sat_b. Each WT reference is the median of valid synonymous cells in its own half. Mean ΔPSI = mean(PSI_mut_a−WT_a, PSI_mut_b−WT_b). For R1A, Δa=0.289803860 and Δb=0.471006817; mean=0.3804053385. PSI(WT)=4.0427815905 and mean mutant PSI=4.423186929. This observation does not validate an E3 mechanism.

slides.title: The task is mutation-effect regression
slides.subtitle: B · This endpoint differs from degron / non-degron classification
slides.notes: Training minimizes MSE; the primary evaluation metric is peptide-macro MAE. Events Δ≥1 and Δ≤−1 support secondary ranking analyses derived from the same regression labels. The model does not directly predict pathogenicity, E3 identity or intact-protein half-life.

items.heading: Input x
items.body: WT sequence of 28 AA, site i and replacement amino acid a. Exactly one substitution generates the mutant.

items.heading: Target y
items.body:
f(x) ≈ ΔPSI = PSI(mutant) − PSI(WT).
Δ > 0: higher reporter stability; Δ < 0: lower reporter stability.

items.heading: Scope
items.body: Sequence-only input; single substitutions in peptide reporters. Measured PSI, read counts and fold IDs are not model features.

slides.title: Five questions organize the progress report
slides.subtitle: B · Current organizing questions; the complete history was not preregistered
slides.notes: These questions organize the implemented protocol and its history. The v3 protocol was written after earlier data/results were known. The prioritization replay is also a post-hoc development analysis.
rows: Does broader training PSI coverage help?
Ridge B/D/E; identical W test population
Does performance transfer or support prioritization?
grouped OOF; calibration; T; replay k10

slides.title: Prior work already addresses several endpoints
slides.subtitle: C · Compare task, data and exposure; published scores use different protocols
slides.notes: Do not claim that previous work only detects motifs or never predicts variant effects: PAP includes ΔPAP and Degformer supports mutant PSI. Author-reported scores on different datasets do not establish matched CT553H performance.
rows: Measured footprints / E3 pairs; primary label source, not CT553H model performance
Abundance prediction and variant follow-up; ΔPAP is not automatically calibrated in ΔPSI units
Transformer PSI prediction, including mutant mode
Training exposure must be audited; the public checkpoint overlaps the benchmark
E3-targeted degron prediction; endpoint differs from substitution ΔPSI

slides.title: Method choices are hypotheses to test
slides.subtitle: C · A scoped evaluation question; absolute novelty is not established
slides.notes: Author/year/DOI metadata follow the bibliography and literature audit of 6 November; selected primary sources were checked online on 7 November. The ESM publisher and OpenReview had access gaps; LoRA arXiv was accessible. This is not a complete systematic review.
rows: Ridge: linear regression with an L2 penalty
Simple control to assess representation value
Frozen embeddings do not guarantee better ΔPSI prediction
LoRA learns low-rank updates to a frozen base
Test rank-8 Q/V adaptation; NLP resource savings do not transfer automatically
Biological case evidence; not the same regression benchmark
Preprint / potential external source; not included in the benchmark

slides.title: From original sources to the v3 data bundle
slides.subtitle: D · Mendeley v2 / GSE240610 → PSI / QC → tables → splits
slides.notes: The label source is Zhang et al. and Mendeley Data version 2, CC BY 4.0. data/README.md records hashes and provenance. Bundle SHA-256: f4a6542f3786de420108861975eae0c58534e5f60a529bce315de9d00bd872a8. The 1 November build is current; the unbuilt specification retained below it in DATASET.md is historical. No data were downloaded again for this presentation.

slides.title: Saturation covers 19 replacements; scanning is sparse
slides.subtitle: D · A mutation cell is a site × amino-acid observation, not a biological cell
slides.notes: Complete saturation yields 28×19=532 nonsynonymous substitutions per peptide. Scanning uses a WT-dependent R/A/S replacement rule, with source-specific C-terminal exceptions; it is not 19 mutants per site. The scanning union has 224,470 cells. Peptide partitions: overlap 1,278; dev 5,489; T 1,414. Only 1,410 T peptides have valid rep1 observations for scoring.

slides.title: Full-PSI training retains technical quality control
slides.subtitle: D · Missing cells are not imputed; test data do not fit quality weights
slides.notes: Reads≥10. Saturation requires at least 10 valid synonymous cells per half; each half uses its own WT median, then matched mutation cells are averaged across halves. Scanning uses the correct replicate-specific _mut0 and retains rep1/rep2/mean12 separately; BAG6 WT is not pooled. Seventeen unmapped scanning peptides are excluded; 45 saturation peptides missing legacy groups are mapped using the full proteome. See the data-method audit and the loader/builder code.

slides.title: A measured mutation matrix for one peptide
slides.subtitle: D · A2RUQ5_C17orf102_2; color shows measured ΔPSI; gray marks WT cells
slides.notes: Select the first peptide by peptide_id rather than a favorable example. The editable matrix is reconstructed from saturation-cells.parquet. Each colored cell is a measured substitution. The display uses a symmetric −3 to +3 PSI palette, saturating extreme colors without altering labels. WT→WT is not a mutation in evaluation.

slides.title: Full-PSI W: 235 peptides, 122,412 mutations
slides.subtitle: D · 221 protein groups; 12,053 cells with Δ≥1 and 1,577 with Δ≤−1
slides.notes: These distributions are calculated directly from the current core table. WT-PSI strata: ≤3:91; (3,4]:85; (4,5]:36; >5:23 peptides. Cells within peptides/proteins are dependent; 122,412 mutation cells are not independent CI units. Neutral cells satisfy −1<Δ<1 and number 108,782.

slides.title: Measurement quality and coverage bound inference
slides.subtitle: D · Ranking metrics use their own eligible-peptide populations
slides.notes: The sequence-only model does not clip predictions using measured WT PSI. Replicate correlation is recorded in the replicate audit cited by output-analysis.json. Rep1 and rep2 are not asserted to have fully verified identical conditions; assay provenance remains separate.

items.heading: Missing measurements
items.body: Not every peptide has all 532 cells. Use QC-passing observations; a missing cell does not mean Δ = 0.

items.heading: Replicate differences
items.body: scan_dev has 152,004 paired rep1/rep2 cells; Pearson r = 0.7074. Disagreement is a quality indicator, not a known variance.

items.heading: Assay floor / ceiling
items.body: 1 − PSI(WT) ≤ ΔPSI ≤ 6 − PSI(WT). WT PSI >5 cannot support a positive event Δ≥1.

slides.title: Protein-group splitting reduces leakage risks
slides.subtitle: D · cov80 + bidirectional cov50 protein hits + exact-sequence unions
slides.notes: The builder combines proteome cov80 groups with MMseqs hits at identity≥0.30, alignment length≥50 AA and bidirectional coverage≥0.50: 12,863 hit edges leave 221 saturation groups. Each group belongs to one outer fold. This heuristic does not exclude every remote homolog or shared motif. Zero additional exact-sequence edges do not prove biological independence.

slides.title: Tune inside; evaluate out of fold outside
slides.subtitle: D / F · 5 outer folds; inner validation ≈20% of groups; seeds 17, 29, 43
slides.notes: Outer-test data do not choose alpha, PCA, epochs or calibration. Arms share inner assignments. Fit transformations on inner-train, select hyperparameters by inner MSE, then reinitialize neural models and refit the eligible outer-train for the selected epochs. OOF predictions come from the fold where the sample/group is held out. Outer-test labels have been inspected during development summaries, so this is not an untouched final test.

slides.title: Five training arms share the full W test set
slides.subtitle: D / F · Arms restrict training only; B still uses high-PSI inner validation
slides.notes: PSI is metadata for constructing views/weights and strata, not an input feature. Arm B does not mean that the whole selection procedure only knows PSI≤4 data. Q1 thresholds for D−B/E−B do not become universal LoRA acceptance thresholds.

slides.title: One data contract, multiple representations
slides.subtitle: E · Data → features / encoder → regression → evaluation → calibration
slides.notes: WT sequence, site i and replacement amino acid form the shared input. Branches include context Ridge, frozen pLM with Ridge or CNN, and frozen/LoRA encoders with newly trained heads. Each predicts ΔPSI; three-class probabilities are calibrated separately. Full fine-tuning is supported by code but has no completed benchmark arm in this campaign.

slides.title: Ridge W5 is an ordered-context baseline
slides.subtitle: E · x ∈ R²⁶⁰ → scaling → Ridge → ΔPSI
slides.notes: features.py builds 40 WT/mutant one-hot features, 20 whole-peptide composition features and 10 ordered neighbors×20 AA=200 features for radius±5, excluding the center: 260 total. Pair+composition has 60 dimensions; unordered context adds 20, giving 80. Fit MSE with an L2 penalty, selecting alpha from {0.1,1,10,100,1000} by inner MSE. This baseline includes positional context, not composition alone.

slides.title: Frozen pLMs represent the WT-to-mutant change
slides.subtitle: E · ESM2-35M: 28 × 480; Δsite + meanΔ gives 960 dimensions
slides.notes: Encode WT and mutant with the same model and remove special tokens, leaving 28 residue vectors. ΔH=Hmut−Hwt. Ridge uses [ΔH at the mutated site; mean ΔH]→PCA64; context models retain the 260-dimensional W5 block separately. Fit scaling/PCA on training data only; PCA uses at most 20,000 seeded training rows. Hidden dimension or published structure performance is not evidence of ΔPSI accuracy.

slides.title: CNNs learn from a crop around the mutation site
slides.subtitle: E · ESM crop ±7: 15 × 480; all modules are verified against code
slides.notes: ConvHead projects Δhidden 480→32 with Linear+GELU. WT one-hot20 and a center indicator add 21 channels, giving 53 per site; padding is masked. Conv k5 with 96 filters→ReLU; global-max96 and center96 pooling are concatenated with auxiliary60, giving 252→Linear64→ReLU/dropout→1. Dropout=0.3; AdamW lr=0.001, weight decay=0.01, batch=256, max 40 epochs, patience 6. mCNN uses kernels 3/5/7 with 32 filters each; pooled total192 and final input252 are retained.

slides.title: Positional-mixing ablation: k1, k5 and multi-scale
slides.subtitle: E / F · Shared crop, auxiliary inputs and splits; parameter counts differ
slides.notes: Artifact head counts are 36,833 for pointwise and 57,185 for CNN on ESM. Different kernel sizes change capacity, so this is not a perfectly parameter-matched isolation of positional mixing. k1 still uses pooling and auxiliary context; it is not a context-free MLP.
rows: No positional mixing in the convolution
k3 / k5 / k7; 32 filters per branch

slides.title: LoRA updates Q/V while preserving base weights
slides.subtitle: E · ESM2-35M; rank 8, alpha 16; frozen and LoRA share the head design
slides.notes: W′=W+(alpha/r)BA. Inject adapters into query/value linear projections only. [Δsite;meanΔ;pair+composition] has 480+480+60=1,020 inputs→MLP64/ReLU/dropout 0.2→1. Frozen training learns the head; LoRA learns adapters and head. Splits, head initialization and backbone eval dropout policy are matched; LoRA gradients remain active. AdamW lr=1e−4, weight decay=0.01, batch 8, gradient clip 1, max 20 epochs, patience 4. This is neither pLM pretraining from scratch nor full fine-tuning.

slides.title: Scanning supports transfer; T stays outside fitting
slides.subtitle: E · scan_dev → 5 pretraining epochs → saturation fine-tuning; scratch control
slides.notes: Stage06 CNN transfer uses one-hot inputs, not ESM+scanning. Ridge source weight is 0.1; quality weights use training disagreement and are capped at 0.1..1. Rep1 and mean12 remain separate arms. scan_overlap is excluded from source training. T is excluded from pretraining, calibration and tuning, but its source was explored historically, so it is not an independent external test.

slides.title: Implemented comparisons retain matched conditions
slides.subtitle: F · OOF / post-hoc development analysis; run and seed details are in Notes
slides.notes: Kaggle run369cb2fe6a1e31e0 contains stages00–06 and stage11 frozen seed17. Local successor ef138c84579c842e completed 633 jobs. External and structure inputs remain pending. Synthetic smoke tests are excluded from scientific benchmark tables.
rows: W folds; full-range validation/test; primary MAE
Matched head / feature conditions within each contrast
Same W cohort; T excluded from fitting
frozen ↔ LoRA; arms B and D
Same runtime, head initialization and splits
Calibrate; lock W5-D before scoring T

slides.title: Three evaluation views answer different questions
slides.subtitle: F · MAE: 235 peptides; AUROC/AP+: 184, AUROC/AP−: 110
slides.notes: RMSE and Spearman are available in the appendix/evidence JSON. Replay recall uses 198 peptides with positive hits; its population differs from AUROC eligibility and full-population precision. Three-class Brier measures squared probability errors; ECE depends on binning.

items.name: MAE ↓
items.meaning: How large are effect-size errors? Calculate MAE within each peptide, then average across peptides.

items.name: AUROC / AP ↑
items.direction: Δ≥1 or Δ≤−1; at least 3 cells in each class
items.meaning: How well are events ranked? AP depends on event prevalence and is not accuracy.

items.name: Precision@10 ↑
items.meaning: How many known hits are found in exactly 10 selections per peptide? Keep peptides with no hits.

slides.title: Resample protein groups, not mutation cells
slides.subtitle: F · 5,000 paired bootstrap draws; ensemble predictions precede metric calculation
slides.notes: Both models use the same sampled groups for paired differences. Folds and seeds share data and are not independent experimental studies. Q1 uses 97.5% Bonferroni intervals for 2 contrasts; matched LoRA uses 98.75% post-hoc intervals for 4; replay uses 97.5% for 2 primary contrasts. Other 95% intervals are descriptive. An interval crossing 0 is unresolved, not evidence of equivalence.

slides.title: What evidence is available as of 7 November?
slides.subtitle: G · Saved 6 November audits; no new model training or scoring in this update
slides.notes: Hashes of presentation input JSON files are checked. The large audit of 4,278 local and 2,986 Kaggle artifacts is cited from saved evidence, not rerun here. All 88 table rows retain their runtime and seed support.

slides.title: Historical results use the same H-sat test set
slides.subtitle: G · H-sat and full-PSI W differ in population, grouping and protocol
slides.notes: Public Degformer training contains 42,163/47,847 mutant cells and WT sequences for all 91 peptides. Cleaned R1 training has already been evaluated. Historical gate/PAP acceptance criteria do not transfer unchanged to LoRA v3. The appendix retains R2/P3/merge/R6/calibration details.

slides.title: Broader training coverage improves Ridge W5
slides.subtitle: G · Identical W test set; peptide-macro MAE ↓; 3-seed prediction ensemble
slides.notes: A/B/C/D/E MAEs are read from output-analysis.json. Q1 retains all 235 test peptides. D−B=−0.025774 and E−B=−0.029963; gains concentrate at high WT PSI. Training coverage and protein groups change together, so this does not isolate a biological mechanism.

slides.title: Q1 improves MAE; the practical margin is unresolved
slides.subtitle: G · 97.5% CIs for D−B/E−B; the −0.02 margin belongs to Q1 only
slides.notes: Adjusted D−B CI=[−0.033806;−0.018286] and E−B=[−0.041656;−0.018817]. Both exclude 0 but are not entirely below −0.02. For WT PSI≤3, AUROC+ D−B95% CI=[−0.002967;+0.001807]; E−B=[−0.010121;−0.001370], reaching losses beyond 0.01. Q1 criteria are not universal LoRA thresholds.

slides.title: Larger pLMs do not yield monotonically lower error
slides.subtitle: G · Frozen pLM + PCA64/Ridge; arm D; same local runtime
slides.notes: Nine checkpoints have actual results, not all 20 registry entries. The plot reports only-D and context-D. Local nested selection reaches MAE 0.394454 and evaluates an inner-fold selection procedure, not an independently validated fixed-family winner. Ankh uses an FP32 encoder; precision policies differ across models, so parameter count alone cannot explain differences.

slides.title: ESM CNN helps; mCNN superiority remains unresolved
slides.subtitle: G · Development; descriptive CIs; k1 and k5 heads differ in parameter count
slides.notes: CNN−pointwise AUROC+ increases by 0.011289.95% CI[0.003434; 0.019133]. One-hot-D CNN−pointwise MAE has a CI crossing 0. CNN is not universally better. CNN-D−B MAE on W has 95% CI[−0.007739;+0.000420], and the low-PSI guardrail is unresolved. mCNN-E versus CNN-D changes both scale and training arm.

slides.title: Scanning pretraining helps its tested control
slides.subtitle: G · One-hot CNN; same W; descriptive 95% CIs; quality weighting worsens MAE
slides.notes: Ridge quality−sat=+0.004010; Ridge scan rep1−sat=−0.003072; CNN pretrain rep1−scratch=−0.006385 and mean12−scratch=−0.006326. Mean12−rep1=+0.000059 has a CI crossing 0. This is not ESM+scanning. Benefits appear in both 20 scanning-type pairs and 360 other pairs, still on saturation development OOF predictions.

slides.title: Learning curves: single fits versus ensembles
slides.subtitle: G · Ridge W5-D; 25/50/75/100% of training groups; fixed W test set
slides.notes: The two series are mean_seed_mae and ensemble_mae from learning_curve. Below 100%, seeds use different subsets, so an ensemble may see a larger union than the nominal fraction of one model. A complete equivalent neural sample-size curve is unavailable. Selected epochs do not replace train/validation loss curves.

slides.title: LoRA improves matched frozen models in B and D
slides.subtitle: G · Matched runtime / head / split; three-seed prediction ensemble
slides.notes: The comparator is the same-runtime stage11 frozen encoder with an MLP head, not the frozen Kaggle CNN-D. MAE uses 235 peptides, AUROC/AP+ on 184 and AUROC/AP− on 110. Each of three seeds lowers MAE and raises AUROC+ against its matched arm. There is no completed full-fine-tuning arm.

slides.title: Group-level intervals support the LoRA gains
slides.subtitle: G · LoRA − frozen; 98.75% post-hoc Bonferroni CIs across four contrasts
slides.notes: The MAE↓ and AUROC+↑ panels read intervals from local-output-analysis.json.contrasts. These are not preregistered confirmatory tests. The intervals are conditional on the available data/split and do not include a new assay source.

slides.title: LoRA-B and D trade off across WT-PSI strata
slides.subtitle: G · Whole-W D−B MAE = +0.00133; 95% CI [−0.00295; +0.00554]
slides.notes: B versus D MAE: le3=0.388442/0.400193; gt3_le4=0.381162/0.381508; gt4_le5=0.309171/0.303302; gt5=0.286305/0.261280. B should not be selected solely by whole-W point rank. Appendix seed results share the outer split and are not three independent studies.

slides.title: Average gains coexist with peptide-level failures
slides.subtitle: G · LoRA-B improves 184/235 peptides; LoRA-D improves 164/235
slides.notes: Each scatter point is a peptide MAE for frozen versus LoRA. B worsens 51 peptides and D worsens 71. The worst LoRA-B peptide, CCDC17 tile9, has MAE 0.9035 versus frozen 0.8486. Positive/negative effect classes have higher MAE than neutral cells. LoRA-B cell-micro signed residuals are −0.9504 for positive and +1.0449 for negative effects, consistent with effect-size shrinkage but not an identified cause. Failure cases remain included.

slides.title: Lower Brier does not improve every calibration metric
slides.subtitle: G · Three-class calibration CV; inner-only; no final LoRA serving model
slides.notes: Three-class Brier averages the summed squared errors of three probabilities; it differs from binary P6. Cell-micro Brier: LoRA-B 0.163071, LoRA-D 0.165899, frozen-B 0.178879, frozen-D 0.179495, inner-prior 0.200569. LoRA ECE+ is higher than frozen for this binning. Reliability bins retain sample counts. Empty model_ids in current cards require provenance completion before serving.

slides.title: Locked T: W5-D only; MAE gain remains unresolved
slides.subtitle: G · 39,234 cells / 1,410 peptides / 730 groups; rep1; R/A/S mutants
slides.notes: W5-D MAE 0.399147 versus zero 0.402403; difference −0.003256.95% CI[−0.009249;+0.002760]. AUROC+=0.840546 on 338 eligible peptides; AUROC−=0.517600 on 85. Three-class Brier micro=0.129119; positive prevalence=0.051155 versus mean predicted probability=0.089529. T shares the lab/source and was historically explored; it is not an independent external test. LoRA has not been evaluated on T.

slides.title: OOF replay uses an equal mutation-selection budget
slides.subtitle: F / G · Primary: LoRA-D ↔ Ridge W5-D ↔ random; k = 10 per peptide
slides.notes: The 235 peptides have 216..532 candidates each; every policy selects 2,350 substitutions. Ranking occurs within each peptide using the three-seed prediction ensemble. Precision retains 37 peptides without positive hits; recall uses 198 with hits. Random uses the analytic expectation of uniform sampling without replacement, not a favorable trial. D was locked for this replay, but models/data had already been explored; this is not independent preregistration.

slides.title: LoRA-D recovers 173 more hits at the same budget
slides.subtitle: G · Positive hit: measured ΔPSI≥1; 2,350 selections per policy
slides.notes: primary_summary gives 1,260 LoRA-D hits,1,087 W5-D hits and 229.857 expected random hits. Peptide-macro precision is 53.6170%,46.2553% and 9.7812%. These are previously measured labels recovered retrospectively, not 1,260 newly validated wet-lab predictions. Frozen-D: 1,124 and LoRA-B: 1,268 are secondary controls and do not reselect the primary recipe.

slides.title: The replay supports a prioritization benefit
slides.subtitle: G · ΔPrecision@10 in percentage points; 97.5% CIs for two primary contrasts
slides.notes: LoRA-D−W5=+7.3617 percentage points, adjusted CI[3.3608; 11.3913]; versus random=+43.8359,[38.6350; 48.8341]. Bootstrap: 5,000 protein groups. Mean selections to recover 50% of known hits: LoRA-D: 71.318; W5: 81.990; random: 255.509 on 198 hit-containing peptides. Total hits are known retrospectively and cannot define a prospective stopping rule. No avoided assays/hours/costs were measured.

slides.title: Replay utility varies across the PSI domain
slides.subtitle: G · Retain all peptides; WT PSI >5 has no observed positive hits
slides.notes: Subgroup results are descriptive and do not replace whole-W findings. Positive Recall@10 is 16.62% for D,13.41% for W5 and 1.93% for random on 198 peptides with hits. LoRA-D−B precision has 95% CI[−2.06;+1.34] percentage points and remains unresolved; keep D as primary. Negative-event evaluation is a separate secondary endpoint.

slides.title: Logged computation is not measured wet-lab cost
slides.subtitle: G · Worker-attempt durations; resumed jobs may omit earlier attempts
slides.notes: Summed durations are neither elapsed campaign time nor GPU-active time. Frozen and LoRA each have 30 B/D×3-seed×5-fold jobs; scheduling and attempt history affect fair cost comparisons. Energy, deployment latency and cost-normalized utility remain unmeasured. No wet-lab monetary savings are inferred.

slides.title: The analysis tool has a baseline; extensions remain open
slides.subtitle: G · Historical software checks do not validate the expanded workflows
slides.notes: Do not promote LoRA to production from development rankings alone. Final refit, export, calibration, inference parity and software acceptance are separate. The slide describes research scope and does not expose internal file paths in the product UI.

slides.title: What do the research questions currently support?
slides.subtitle: H · Provisional synthesis; favorable and unfavorable results are retained
slides.notes: Lack of a new architecture does not imply lack of contribution. The protocol allows methodological, benchmark, evaluation and software contributions. Development improvements do not themselves create a G2/G3 acceptance decision.

slides.title: Scientific limits accompany every result
slides.subtitle: H · External / structure inputs remain pending; published results cannot fill them
slides.notes: Available results do not establish final scientific novelty. The literature review has scope/access limits and cannot support a first-ever claim. Final model export and clinical inference are outside the current evidence.

items.heading: Generalization
items.body: Grouping is heuristic. Assays/labs are related; peptide context differs from native proteins.

items.heading: Model selection
items.body: Many recipes have been inspected on development data. Post-hoc CIs do not include new splits or assays.

items.heading: Practical utility
items.body: Replay utility is retrospective. CT553H has no prospective wet-lab, half-life, E3 or measured monetary/time benefit.

slides.title: Progress conclusions remain open to revision
slides.subtitle: H · Provisional conclusions; not an acceptance record
slides.notes: This structure can become a final conclusion when appropriate evidence and decisions are available. Do not use a best-model or cost-saved template. Methodological and empirical contributions do not require claiming a novel architecture.

items.heading: Completed work
items.body: Traceable labels, QC and splits; Ridge–pLM–CNN–LoRA controls; 88 v3 recipes and an equal-budget replay.

items.heading: Current support
items.body: LoRA improves matched frozen models on W. LoRA-D recovers more positive hits than W5/random in development replay.

items.heading: Not yet decided
items.body: No final production model or overall conclusion. The G2 dossier is ready for review; no closure decision is recorded.

slides.title: Next steps should answer explicit questions
slides.subtitle: H · Proposed work; this presentation update runs no training or wet-lab experiment
slides.notes: (1) Confirm the current G2 scope/criteria and record the student/supervisor decision. (2) Lock recipe and intended domain before further evaluation; do not select on inspected T. (3) Audit a new compatible source for homology, assay, errors and calibration. (4) Refit/export with tokenizer/precision/calibrator provenance and inference parity, then assess G3. (5) For real utility claims, run controlled prospective selection and measure resources. Pending branches are not automatically universal requirements for recognizing development contributions.
